abstract: We prove a sharp positive-comparison theorem for finite-rank self-adjoint decompositions $A=P+Q$ with $P\ge0$ and a global inertia bound on $Q$. The complete level-two remainder controls the squared Hilbert--Schmidt distance to an operator $0\le C\le2I$ that retains the simple-count cubic inequality. Both the cap two and the distance coefficient one are optimal in this abstract class. Positivity of this comparison yields a stronger continuous triangular cubic stability estimate requiring an ordered fourth moment, without a full fourth spectral moment. We combine these operator results with the previously proved unconditional ordered moments and height approximation of Paper 155, and with the unchanged J21 certificate, to obtain $\liminf N_0^s(T)/N(T)\ge0.673856$. A one-dimensional majorant reduces the ordered fourth-moment constant to finite rational Fourier calculations; Arb certifies the final contradiction with margin greater than $0.00010447207117880$. Finite matrix, continuous triangle, and quadrature controls support the algebra and normalizations. The original certificate admissibility and analytic moment theorems are explicitly imported. The numerical gain is small; the main contribution is the optimal positive comparison and the stronger remainder constraint it permits. This is a partial result about zeros on the critical line, not a resolution of the Riemann hypothesis.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Recast the scope-rejected Paper155 revision as one focused follow-up, as requested. The accepted ordered-moment and height-transfer theorems are explicitly cited and restated as inputs; their full proofs are removed. Retain one combined contribution: the optimal cap-two comparison, positive cubic estimate, one-dimensional majorant, and .673856 consequence. Add a short exact example establishing sharpness of the cap and distance coefficient. No individual auxiliary ingredient is submitted separately.
title: A sharp positive comparison for the zero-frame remainder
